work.text: Pope Paul III and His Grandsons ranks as one of Titian's finest and most penetrating works. Although unfinished and less technically accomplished than his Portrait of Pope Paul III of a few years earlier, it is renowned for its rich colouring; the deep reds of the tablecloth and the almost spectral whites of Paul's gown.

work.lead: Claude Phillips on the Naples group, 1898:

moment.text: rooms were given to him in the Belvedere, to the end that he might set his hand to painting once more the portrait of Pope Paul, of full length, with one of Farnese and one of Duke Ottavio, which he executed excellently well and much to the satisfaction of those lords.

moment.lead: Visiting Titian in the Belvedere, Michelangelo praised his Danaë to Vasari, with a reservation:

moment.text: I recollect hearing Messer Titian say when I visited his house in my childhood to learn something of painting that he had greatly improved his works after having been in Rome

source.author: Giovanni Battista Leoni
source.title: Letter to Francesco Montemezzano, Rome, 6 August 1589 (in Lettere familiari, 1600)

matters.text: The painting explores the effects of ageing and the manoeuvring behind succession; Paul was at the time in his late seventies and ruling in an uncertain political climate as Charles V, Holy Roman Emperor came into ascendancy.

source.author: Wikipedia contributors
source.title: Pope Paul III and His Grandsons

matters.text: Aware of the changing tides of influence, Titian abandoned the commission before completion, and for the next 100 years the painting languished unframed in a Farnese cellar.
